subject.title: feat(channels): add typed cross-surface approval actions

question: Should an authorized approval.resolve request with the wrong explicit owner kind terminally deny the canonical pending approval, or reject without mutation?
rationale: Both behaviors are defensible fail-closed policies, but the choice changes how stale or incorrectly encoded callbacks affect executable approval state and cannot be inferred safely from tests alone.

options.title: Reject without mutation
options.body: Return approval-not-found or invalid-request for a kind mismatch while leaving the pending approval unchanged.

options.title: Terminally deny
options.body: Keep kind mismatch in the malformed-verdict path so any authenticated mismatch closes the approval as denied.

recommendation.title: Reject without mutation
recommendation.body: Return approval-not-found or invalid-request for a kind mismatch while leaving the pending approval unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: The current resolver behavior and durable approval design originate in this person's recent merged history.
